activePlan.objective: Add a periodic 'still running' heartbeat to the workload runner, per the owner's explicit request, so a long-running Crucible command doesn't look hung.
steps: Add workload.heartbeatSeconds (bounded 5-300, default 60) to .thecrucible.schema.json and src/config.js's validated defaults.
In src/runner.js's runCommand, start a setInterval immediately after spawning the child process and clear it on close/error/timeout, so it can only fire while that exact command is actively running.
Thread config.workload.heartbeatSeconds through runCrucible's prepare and verify command loops.
Document the new field in templates/thecrucible.example.json and README's workload section.
Add tests: bounds validation, a real heartbeat firing multiple times during an artificially slow command, and zero heartbeats for a command that finishes before the interval elapses.
Run the full local suite plus every fast/offline audit before pushing.

completed: Added workload.heartbeatSeconds to the schema and validated config (bounded 5-300, default 60).

runCommand now emits '[The Crucible] Still running: <command> (Ns elapsed)' to stdout on that interval, started only after the child process spawns and cleared the instant it closes, errors, or times out - never an idle tick, only while a command is genuinely running.
Documented the new field in templates/thecrucible.example.json and README's ### workload section and feature-bullet list.
verification: Proved the heartbeat fires multiple times for an artificially slow command and never fires for one that finishes before the interval elapses.
lint:workflows, docs:check, validate, audit:clutter, audit:privacy, and audit:security all pass.
